statement: In a given square to inscribe a circle.
heath_proof: Let ABCD be the given square; thus it is required to inscribe a circle in the given square ABCD. Let the straight lines AD, AB be bisected at the points E, F respectively [I. 10], through E let EH be drawn parallel to either AB or CD, and through F let FK be drawn parallel to either AD or BC; [I. 31] therefore each of the figures AK, KB, AH, HD, AG, GC, BG, GD is a parallelogram, and their opposite sides are evidently equal. [I. 34] Now, since AD is equal to AB, and AE is half of AD, and AF half of AB, therefore AE is equal to AF, so that the opposite sides are also equal;  therefore FG is equal to GE. Similarly we can prove that each of the straight lines GH, GK is equal to each of the straight lines FG, GE; therefore the four straight lines GE, GF, GH, GK are equal to one another. Therefore the circle described with centre G and distance one of the straight lines GE, GF, GH, GK will pass also through the remaining points. And it will touch the straight lines AB, BC, CD, DA, because the angles at E, F, H, K are right. For, if the circle cuts AB, BC, CD, DA, the straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of the circle from its extremity will fall within the circle: which was proved absurd; [III. 16] therefore the circle described with centre G and distance one of the straight lines GE, GF, GH, GK will not cut the straight lines AB, BC, CD, DA. Therefore it will touch them, and will have been inscribed in the square ABCD. Therefore in the given square a circle has been inscribed.

**Statement:** In a given square to inscribe a circle.

**Step 1.** Let ABCD be the given square, with vertices labeled so that AB, BC, CD, DA are its sides and all angles are right angles [D1.22].

**Step 2.** Bisect side AD at point E, and bisect side BC at point F [1.10]. Then AE = ED and BF = FC.

**Step 3.** Join EF [P1]. Since ABCD is a square, it is a parallelogram, so AD is parallel to BC and AD = BC [1.34]. Since AE = half of AD, and BF = half of BC, and AD = BC, we have AE = BF. Also AB is parallel to DC [1.34]. Now ABFE has AB parallel to EF (since AE = BF and AE is parallel to BF, AEFB is a parallelogram by 1.33), so EF is parallel to AB and EF = AB [1.34].

**Step 4.** Bisect EF at point K [1.10]. Then EK = KF.

**Step 5.** Through K, draw KL parallel to AD (and hence to BC), meeting AB at L and DC at M [1.31].

**Step 6.** Since ABFE is a parallelogram and EF is parallel to AB, with KL parallel to AE, the figure AEKL is a parallelogram. Therefore KL = AE and LK is parallel to AE [1.34]. Similarly, EKFB is a parallelogram, and LKFB is a parallelogram with KL = BF [1.34]. But AE = BF, confirming KL = AE.

**Step 7.** Since AEKL is a parallelogram, AL = EK [1.34]. Since LKFB is a parallelogram, LB = KF [1.34]. Since EK = KF (Step 4), we have AL = LB, so L is the midpoint of AB.

**Step 8.** Similarly, since DEKM is a parallelogram (DK parallel to EM by construction, DE parallel to KM), we have DM = EK and KM = DE [1.34]. And since KMFC is a parallelogram, MC = KF and KM = FC [1.34]. Since EK = KF, we have DM = MC, so M is the midpoint of DC.

**Step 9.** Now we establish that KE = KL = KF = KM. We have EK = KF (Step 4). Since AEKL is a parallelogram, KL = AE [1.34]. Since the square has all sides equal, AD = AB [D1.22]. Since AE = half of AD (Step 2) and AL = half of AB (Step 7), we have AE = AL. But KL = AE, so KL = AE = AL. Also EK = AL [1.34 applied to parallelogram AEKL], giving EK = KL. Since EK = KF (Step 4), and KL = AE = EK, and by the same reasoning KM = DE = AE = EK, we have KE = KF = KL = KM.

**Step 10.** Since KL is parallel to AD and angle DAB is a right angle [D1.22], the angle ALK is a right angle [1.29]. That is, KL is perpendicular to AB at L. Similarly, since EF is parallel to AB and angle DAB is a right angle, the angle AEF is a right angle [1.29], so KE is perpendicular to AD at E. By the same reasoning, KF is perpendicular to BC at F [1.29], and KM is perpendicular to DC at M [1.29].

**Step 11.** Describe the circle with center K and radius KE [P3]. Since KE = KF = KL = KM (Step 9), the points E, F, L, M all lie on this circle [D1.15].

**Step 12.** Since KE is perpendicular to AD at E, and E lies on the circle, the line AD meets the circle at E and, being perpendicular to the radius KE at E, does not cut the circle but touches it [3.16]. Therefore side AD is tangent to the circle at E.

**Step 13.** By the same reasoning, since KL is perpendicular to AB at L and KL is a radius, side AB touches the circle at L [3.16]. Since KF is perpendicular to BC at F and KF is a radius, side BC touches the circle at F [3.16]. Since KM is perpendicular to DC at M and KM is a radius, side DC touches the circle at M [3.16].

**Step 14.** Therefore the circle with center K and radius KE is inscribed in the square ABCD, since its circumference touches each side of the square [D4.5]. This is what was required to do.
